docs.title: SAM One-Click
docs.text:
Select a person, a product or any object in one step. Tell the node roughly where it is and Segment Anything draws a clean selection around it, like the Object Selection tool in Photoshop.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → mask → Mask: SAM One-Click Good for Selecting a subject for a background swap, isolating a product, building a first mask that you then refine for hair Speed At 2048 × 1365 on an RTX 5090: vit_b about 0.2 s and 2.9 GB of VRAM, mobile_sam about 0.04 s and 0.35 GB. mobile_sam on CPU takes about 1.5 s. The first run also loads the model.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Segment Anything (SAM) is a model from Meta that has learned what "an object" looks like. You do not paint the selection. You give it a hint and it finds the edges.

ComfyUI has no "click on the image" widget, so the hint is text. You have three ways to give it:

  • Points. Type the position of a pixel on the object, for example [[1200, 700]]. Add points that must stay out in negative_points_json.
  • A face box. Connect bbox_json from Face Detect or Face Detect Lite.
  • A rough mask. Connect any MASK to mask_hint. The node uses its bounding box and a point inside it.

If you give nothing, the node clicks the middle of the image.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Load Image → Mask: SAM One-Click.
  2. In points_json type one point on your subject, such as [[0.5, 0.45]] (see below for the two ways to write coordinates).
  3. Connect preview to a Preview Image node. The selection is tinted red with an outline.
  4. Not right? Add a point on a missing part to points_json, or a point on something that leaked in to negative_points_json.

docs.title: How to "click"
docs.text:
Points in pixels. [[x, y], [x, y]] with the origin at the top-left corner. Read the position from any image viewer. Valid values run from 0 to width − 1 and 0 to height − 1; a point on or past the edge (for example x equal to the width) is rejected.

Points as a fraction of the image. If every number is between 0 and 1 and at least one of them is a real fraction (such as 0.5), the node reads them as fractions: [[0.5, 0.4]] is the middle horizontally and 40 % down. This is handy because it works at any resolution. A list made only of 0 and 1, like [[1, 1]] or [[0, 0]], is read as pixels, because it cannot be told apart from pixel 1 or pixel 0.

Only negative points. Allowed, but SAM then has nothing to select and the result is unreliable. The node writes a warning to the log. Add a positive point, a box or a mask hint.

From a face. Connect bbox_json from Face Detect. The node reads the list of {x, y, w, h, ...} boxes. With a batch of images it picks the box whose batch_index matches each image. If the boxes carry no batch_index the first one is used.

From a rough mask. Draw a loose mask (even a rectangle) or take one from another node and connect it to mask_hint. SAM tightens it to the real edges.

You can combine them. A face box plus one point on the shoulder is a common mix.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Tip model vit_b Which Segment Anything model to use. mobile_sam for speed, vit_h for the cleanest edges. points_json empty Positive points on the object. One to three points are usually enough. negative_points_json empty Points on things that must not be selected. Use it to cut a chair or a hand out of the mask. multimask on SAM proposes 3 masks and the one with the best predicted score is kept. Leave on for a single click. Turn off when you give a box or several points. mask_threshold 0.0 Cut-off for the final mask. Below 0 grows the mask, above 0 shrinks it. Try ±1. bbox_json (optional) empty Face box from Face Detect / Face Detect Lite. Connect the output, do not type it. mask_hint (optional) none A rough mask. A box-shaped mask is enough. keep_model_loaded (optional) on Keep the SAM model in VRAM between runs. Turn off to free 0.4–7 GB right after the run; ComfyUI's Free memory button does not reach this model.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Type Meaning mask MASK The selection: 1 inside, 0 outside. One mask per image. score FLOAT SAM's own quality estimate (about 0 to 1). With a batch, the average. Below 0.7 means you should add a point. preview IMAGE The image with the mask tinted and outlined, for checking.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
The files go in ComfyUI/models/sams/. A missing file is downloaded the first time you use that model.

Model File Size VRAM (about) Notes vit_b sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth 375 MB 3 GB Default. Good balance. mobile_sam mobile_sam.pt 39 MB 0.4 GB Fastest, fine on CPU. Less precise on busy backgrounds. vit_l sam_vit_l_0b3195.pth 1.2 GB 5 GB (estimate) Large download. vit_h sam_vit_h_4b8939.pth 2.5 GB 7 GB (estimate) Large download. Best quality.

Only one model stays loaded. Switching model frees the previous one from VRAM. The folder follows extra_model_paths.yaml when a sams entry exists there. Downloads have a timeout, are written to a .part file first, and vit_b and mobile_sam are checked against their SHA256 (no official hash is published for vit_l and vit_h, so only their size is checked).

Segment Anything and MobileSAM are released under the Apache-2.0 licence, which allows commercial use.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• A single click on a large subject can pick only a part (a face but not the body). Add a second positive point on the other part, or switch multimask off and add a box.
  • For portraits a face box is a good start but it covers only the face. Add a point on the torso, or feed a rough body mask to mask_hint.
  • SAM's edge is clean but binary. For hair and fur chain it into Sub-Pixel Mask Refiner, or build a Trimap and feed Alpha Matte for real soft hair.
  • Use preview while you place points, then take mask for the real work.
  • Very large images are resized inside the model (1024 px on the long side) and the mask is scaled back up. Fine hair detail will not come from SAM alone.
Under the hood

The node uses Kornia's VisualPrompter with the Sam model. The image (range 0 to 1) is resized so its long side is 1024, normalised and run through the image encoder once per image. Points go in as labelled keypoints (1 positive, 0 negative), a box as an xyxy box, in original pixel coordinates; Kornia scales them to the model frame.

The decoder returns up to 3 low-resolution logit maps with a predicted IoU each. The best by predicted IoU is upsampled to the original size, then cut at mask_threshold (a logit, 0 is SAM's default).

A mask hint adds its bounding box (unless bbox_json already gives one) and a positive point at the centroid, moved to the nearest mask pixel if the centroid falls outside the mask. With multimask on, candidate masks that cover more than 90 % of the image are skipped unless every candidate does. One model is cached at a time (the previous one is evicted on a change of model or device); it runs on CUDA when available, otherwise CPU. Each image in a batch is encoded separately.

docs.text:

docs.text: SAM One-Click Mask example workflow feeds Face Detect Lite's box into SAM, then fills holes with Mask Cleanup and shows the cutout. It uses only core ComfyUI nodes and this pack. Copy workflows/sample_portrait.jpg into ComfyUI/input/.

docs.title: Saturation Mask
docs.text:
Selects pixels by how vivid they are, not by where they are. Use it to grab only the loud colours, only the dull ones, or everything in between.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → color → Saturation Mask Builder Good for Taming oversaturated clothing or backgrounds, boosting only dull areas, protecting already-vivid colours from a grade

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Saturation is how strong a colour is: a neon sign is highly saturated, a grey wall has almost none. A saturation mask works like a luminosity mask (a selection made from brightness), but it follows colour strength instead.

Typical uses:

  • Pull down only the over-saturated reds in a dress without touching skin.
  • Lift only the flat, washed-out areas.
  • Feed the mask into any node that accepts a MASK, such as LUT Import, so a grade only lands where you want it.

The value is measured as HLS saturation (hue, lightness, saturation), the same idea as the saturation slider in most editors.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Connect Load Image → Saturation Mask Builder.
  2. Leave sat_min at 0.30 and sat_max at 1.00 to select the vivid part of the picture.
  3. Connect the mask output to Mask Preview to see the selection, or to the mask input of another node.
  4. Move sat_min up to narrow the selection to only the strongest colours.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip sat_min 0.30 Lowest saturation that is included (0 to 1). Raise it to ignore dull areas. sat_max 1.00 Highest saturation that is included (0 to 1). Must be larger than sat_min. Lower it to leave the most vivid colours out. feather 0.10 Softness of the edges around both limits (0 to 1). 0 gives a hard on/off mask; 0.05 to 0.15 avoids visible steps.

Output: mask — a MASK with values from 0 (not selected) to 1 (fully selected), one per image in the batch.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Keep some feather. A hard threshold on saturation produces blotchy, noisy selections on skin and fabric.
  • To protect already-vivid colours, select a low range (for example sat_min 0, sat_max 0.4) and apply your grade through that mask.
  • Skin sits in a middle saturation band. If a grade is affecting skin, combine this mask with a hue selection using Hue/Saturation per Range.
  • Clean up speckles with Mask Cleanup before using the mask on a final export.
Under the hood

The image is converted to HLS and the saturation channel is compared with the range. With feather at 0 the result is a binary mask. Otherwise each limit gets a smoothstep ramp of width feather (the lower ramp ends at sat_min, the upper ramp starts at sat_max), and the two are multiplied. sat_max must be strictly greater than sat_min, otherwise the node raises an error. The same function drives the saturation step inside some Look Select presets.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Hue/Saturation per Range — adjust colour inside a hue band.
  • Luminosity Masking — the brightness-based equivalent.
  • Mask Combine — multiply or add this mask with other selections.
  • Look Select — uses saturation masks inside some looks.

docs.text: Selective color example workflow. It builds a Saturation Mask from the portrait, shows it as a heatmap, and uses Hue/Saturation per Range on one colour band. Copy workflows/sample_portrait.jpg into ComfyUI/input/. It uses only core ComfyUI nodes and this pack.

docs.title: Shadows/Highlights Pro
docs.text:
Lifts the shadows and recovers the highlights of a picture without the flat, grey "cheap HDR" look. Choose between a Camera Raw–style model that leaves no halos and the classic Photoshop Shadows/Highlights dialog.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → color → Color: Shadows/Highlights Pro Good for Backlit portraits, opening up dark faces and hair, taming bright skies and windows, cutting shine on skin Speed About 0.1 s per 4K image on a CUDA GPU after warm-up, peak VRAM under 1 GB. About 14 s at 4K on the CPU.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Use it when the light in a photo is right but the tonal range is too wide: a face in shade against a bright background, a dark jacket with no detail, or a sky that is almost white. A plain curve or exposure change moves every pixel; this node looks at each area's surroundings, so it lifts what is dark compared with its neighbourhood and calms what is bright, while keeping local contrast.

There are two models:

  • camera_raw works like the Shadows and Highlights sliders in Lightroom / Camera Raw. Both sliders work in both directions, hard edges keep no halo (a bright or dark rim around objects), and colours are kept because only brightness is changed. On grey test charts it comes close to published Photoshop 25.4 Camera Raw measurements (Shadows +100: 165.2 against 165.3 of 255; Highlights -100: 90.4 against 89.6). Treat it as a close model, not an exact copy of Lightroom or Photoshop on every photo.
  • photoshop follows Image > Adjustments > Shadows/Highlights, with its Tone, Radius, Color and Midtone controls. Like the dialog, it can only lift shadows and darken highlights.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Load Image → Color: Shadows/Highlights Pro → Preview Image.
  2. Keep mode on camera_raw and start from the defaults (shadows 30, highlights -30).
  3. Raise shadows until the dark areas show detail; lower highlights until the sky or skin shine looks right.
  4. Optional: connect a mask to mask to limit the change to the subject or the sky.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip shadows 30 -100 to 100. Positive lifts dark areas relative to their surroundings; negative deepens them (camera_raw only). 20 to 50 for portraits; up to 100 for strong backlight. highlights -30 -100 to 100. Negative recovers bright areas (skies, windows, skin shine); positive brightens them (camera_raw only). -20 to -60 for most photos. mode camera_raw camera_raw = Lightroom / Camera Raw style sliders, no halos. photoshop = the Image > Adjustments > Shadows/Highlights model. Start with camera_raw; use photoshop when you want the dialog's controls. mask (optional) none Limits where the effect applies (1 = full effect, 0 = untouched, soft values blend). Must match the image size; a one-image mask applies to the whole batch. Use a subject, sky or Luminosity Masking mask. ps_shadow_tone 50 Photoshop mode. Tonal width of the shadows (0–100 %): how far up the tones the shadow lift reaches. Lower it to touch only the deepest shadows. ps_shadow_radius 30 Photoshop mode. Shadows neighbourhood size in pixels (0–2500). Larger radius on large images; small values look more local and crunchy. ps_highlight_tone 50 Photoshop mode. Tonal width of the highlights (0–100 %). Lower it to touch only the brightest areas. ps_highlight_radius 30 Photoshop mode. Highlights neighbourhood size in pixels (0–2500). Same as the shadow radius. ps_color 20 Photoshop mode. Saturation in the adjusted tones (-100 to 100). Raise it if lifted shadows look washed out; lower it if they look too colourful. ps_midtone 0 Photoshop mode. Midtone contrast (-100 to 100). Small positive values bring back punch after a strong lift.

The ps_ settings are ignored in camera_raw mode.

Output

Output What it is image The adjusted image, same size as the input. With both sliders at 0 it is the input, unchanged.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• In camera_raw, highlights also lowers the whole picture slightly, because the darkest content is kept in place, as in Camera Raw. Add a little exposure afterwards in ColorLab if needed.
  • In photoshop mode, negative shadows and positive highlights do nothing: the dialog cannot darken shadows or brighten highlights. With shadows at 0 or below and highlights at 0 or above, the image passes through unchanged, so ps_color and ps_midtone alone have no effect.
  • The node turns off the Photoshop dialog's Black Clip / White Clip stretch, so lifted shadows are not pushed back to black.
  • Very strong values flatten the picture. Bring depth back with CLAHE Local Contrast or a gentle S-curve in Tone Curve.
  • For a backlit portrait, mask the subject so the bright background keeps its airy look.
Under the hood

camera_raw: the image is converted to linear RGB and its Rec. 709 luminance to log2 (stops). A fast local Laplacian filter (Paris, Hasinoff & Kautz 2011, in the fast form of Aubry et al. 2014, reference values 1/8 stop apart) runs on a proxy whose long edge is at most 1600 px. Highlights pull pixels brighter than their surroundings towards them past a small detail threshold, and the 1st percentile is put back; Shadows raise pixels darker than their surroundings, and the 99th percentile is put back. The change is carried to full size by a fast guided upsampling, then applied as a gain on linear RGB, so hue is kept and the look does not depend on image size.

photoshop: neighbourhood brightness is an edge-aware average of (max(R,G,B) + luma) / 2 (Gaussian sigma about 1.14 × Radius). Tonal masks are the complement of a Beta CDF whose shape moves with Tone; the curve strength follows Amount; Color re-adds the pixel's colour difference scaled and kept in gamut; Midtone is a global S-curve. It works on sRGB values, as Photoshop does in an sRGB document.

The strength knots, Beta mask table, Color and Midtone tables are translated from PhotoCraft (MIT License, see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), which fitted them to Photoshop 25.4 by black-box measurement.

ComfyUI hands images over on the CPU; the node moves the work to the GPU when one exists and falls back to the CPU on out-of-memory. The optional mask blends the result with the original. Source: core/shadows_highlights.py, core/local_laplacian.py, core/shadows_highlights_ps.py.

docs.text:
• ColorLab for exposure, white balance and the rest of a basic grade
  • Luminosity Masking to build a shadows or highlights mask
  • CLAHE Local Contrast to add local punch back
  • Tone Curve for global contrast after the lift

docs.text: Shadows/Highlights Pro example workflow opens up the shadows and recovers the highlights of the sample portrait. It uses only core ComfyUI nodes and this pack. Copy workflows/sample_portrait.jpg into ComfyUI/input/.

docs.title: Skin Tone Tri-Region
docs.text:
Splits a portrait into three soft masks: the darker skin tones, the middle ones and the brightest ones. Use them to retouch shadows, midtones and highlights of the skin independently.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → face → Face: Skin Tone Tri-Region Good for Taming shine on highlights; lifting or warming shadows; grading the main skin tone; targeted dodge and burn

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Skin rarely needs the same fix everywhere. Highlights need shine control, shadows may need lifting or warming, and midtones carry the main skin colour. A luminosity mask (a mask built from how bright each pixel is) lets you target one of those ranges. This node builds three of them in one step and makes sure they add up cleanly.

Feed it an optional skin mask so that hair, clothing and background do not take part in the split. Without one, the whole frame is split by brightness.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Connect Load Image to image.
  2. Optional but recommended: connect a skin-only mask (from a person or skin segmentation node) to skin_mask.
  3. Send highlight_mask, midtone_mask or shadow_mask to the mask input of whatever adjustment you want to limit, for example Face Beauty Blend, a colour node or a LUT.
  4. Start with the default cutoffs and adjust them to your image.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Tip image — The portrait to analyse. skin_mask optional Limits the split to skin. Without it the whole frame is split. A good mask gives much cleaner results than the whole frame. shadow_cutoff 0.33 (0–0.5) Brightness below this counts as shadow. Lower it to shrink the shadow mask. highlight_cutoff 0.66 (0.5–1) Brightness above this counts as highlight. Raise it to keep only the brightest shine. soft_sigma 1.0 (0–8) Softens the boundaries between the three ranges. Raise for gentler transitions between ranges. 0 gives hard edges. Output Type Meaning shadow_mask MASK Darker skin tones. midtone_mask MASK Middle skin tones. highlight_mask MASK Brightest skin tones.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• The cutoff shadow_cutoff must be lower than highlight_cutoff; the node rejects other combinations.
  • On a very dark or very bright portrait, move both cutoffs together so each mask still has a useful share of the face.
  • The three masks always add up to your skin mask (or to a full white frame when none is connected), so nothing is lost or counted twice.
  • Use highlight_mask for specular shine and highlight colour; midtone_mask for the main skin grade; shadow_mask for lifting and noise control.
  • Preview a mask with Mask Preview before using it.
Under the hood

Brightness is Rec. 601 luma, 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B, computed from the clamped image. Hard masks are made from the two cutoffs, multiplied by the skin mask, blurred with a separable Gaussian (replicate padding), then renormalised so the three add up to the skin mask. Cutoffs must satisfy 0 ≤ shadow < highlight ≤ 1, with shadow ≤ 0.5 and highlight ≥ 0.5. skin_mask must match the image height and width. The code lives in core/skin_tone_region.py.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Face Beauty Blend — blend a retouch through one of these masks.
  • Luminosity Masking — more flexible brightness masks for any image.
  • Mask Combine — combine these masks with other masks.
  • Face category overview

docs.title: Example workflow
docs.text: Skin Tone Tri-Region example workflow. It uses the person-mask node of the external A Person Mask Generator pack (install it separately) to create the skin mask. See the Skin Tone Retouch example for a full walkthrough.

docs.title: Sky Mask
docs.text:
Selects the sky for you: blue, overcast or sunset. Use the mask to grade the sky on its own, swap it, or protect it from other edits.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → mask → Mask: Sky Good for Grading or replacing the sky, darkening a bright sky, keeping the sky out of a skin or foreground edit Speed About 0.2 s per photo

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Selecting a sky by hand means a gradient mask plus a lot of cleaning around trees and roofs. This node does it from the picture itself. It needs no AI model and no download.

It looks for three things: sky colour (blue, white or grey cloud, and warm sunset glow), a smooth surface (sky has little fine texture), and a position open to the top of the frame. Leaves, buildings and grass fail the smoothness test. A white wall low in the frame fails the position test.

The mask is soft. Edges around branches and roof lines follow the real edge, so a grade applied through the mask does not leave a halo.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Load Image → Mask: Sky.
  2. Add Mask Preview to see the mask over the photo.
  3. Keep sensitivity at 0.5 and refine_edges on.
  4. To grade only the sky, connect sky_mask to the mask input of Apply ColorLab Preset.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip image Photo with sky. sensitivity 0.5 0 to 1. Higher also takes hazy, textured or sunset sky. Lower keeps only clear sky. Raise it for thin cloud or sunset. Lower it if walls or water leak in. refine_edges on Follows branches and roof lines at full resolution with a colour-guided filter. Turn off only if you want a plain soft mask.

Output

Output What it is sky_mask Soft mask of the sky. White is sky. One mask per photo in the batch.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Check the mask with Mask Preview before you grade. Raise sensitivity in small steps until hazy or sunset areas are covered.
  • Calm water that joins the sky at the horizon can be included. Draw or build a mask for the water and subtract it with Mask Combine.
  • White, smooth walls that touch the sky can leak a little. Lower sensitivity, or clean up with Mask Cleanup.
  • Very textured clouds need a higher sensitivity because they look less smooth.
  • Use the inverted mask to protect the sky while you edit the rest, for example with Color Matcher or a Layer node.
Under the hood

The photo is reduced to a copy of at most 768 px on the long edge. On it, a sky score combines colour (blue by hue and saturation, bright near-grey for cloud, and warm bright upper areas at half weight for sunset) with a smoothness test on local luma variation. A higher sensitivity lowers the score threshold and relaxes the smoothness test.

Candidate regions are kept only if they are connected to the top rows of the frame, or are large and in the upper half. When little sky reaches the top (looking up through branches), large clearly blue regions anywhere are kept too. Small gaps such as birds and wires are closed first.

With refine_edges, the mask is scaled back to full size and refined with a colour guided filter on the original photo. Source: core/sky_mask.py, wrapper nodes/sky_mask_node.py.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Apply ColorLab Preset: grade only the masked sky
  • Mask Combine: add or subtract masks, for example to remove water
  • Mask Cleanup: remove specks and fill holes
  • Mask Preview: check the mask over the photo

docs.text: Sky Mask example workflow finds the sky of an architecture photo, shows it with Mask Preview, and applies a ColorLab preset only to the sky through the mask. Copy workflows/sample_architecture.jpg into ComfyUI/input/ (Pexels License).

docs.title: Smart Sharpen
docs.text:
Makes edges and texture crisper with an unsharp mask. A threshold keeps noise and grain from being boosted, it sharpens brightness only by default so colours do not fringe, and an optional mask lets you sharpen only the areas you choose.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → filters → Filters: Smart Sharpen Good for Final output sharpening, bringing back eyes and hair detail, sharpening textured areas while leaving skin and sky smooth

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Unsharp mask is the same idea as Photoshop's Unsharp Mask: blur a copy, subtract it from the original to find the detail, and add that detail back with extra strength.

Use this node as one of the last steps, after smoothing, colour work and any resize.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Load Image → Filters: Smart Sharpen → Preview Image.
  2. Start with amount = 1.0, radius = 1.0, threshold = 0.
  3. For grainy images, raise threshold to about 0.02 to 0.05.
  4. To sharpen only detail areas, connect a mask from Detail Mask to mask.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip amount 1.0 (0 to 5) Strength. 0 returns the image unchanged. 0.5 to 1 is usually enough. Above 2 expect halos. radius 1.0 (0.3 to 10) Size of the detail that gets boosted, in pixels (blur sigma). 0.5 to 1 for fine detail and web size, 1.5 to 3 for large prints. Above 5 acts like local contrast. threshold 0.0 (0 to 0.5) Detail weaker than this is left alone. Raise it to avoid boosting noise or film grain. luminance_only on Sharpen brightness only, leave colour as it is. Keep on to avoid coloured edges. mask (optional) none Where sharpening applies: white = full, black = none. Batch of 1 is reused for all images.

Output: image, the sharpened picture (IMAGE).

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Sharpen after Skin Smoother, never before, or you will sharpen the blemishes you are about to smooth.
  • A mask of eyes, lashes, hair and fabric gives crisp detail without making skin look rough.
  • The image must be larger than ceil(3 × radius) pixels on both sides, or the node reports an error.
  • Use QA Image Diff to check that sharpening only changed what you intended.
Under the hood

detail = x − gaussian_blur(x, sigma = radius) with reflect borders and a kernel of 2 × ceil(3 × radius) + 1. The detail is soft-thresholded, sign(d) × max(|d| − threshold, 0), which is a smooth ramp so no speckle appears at the cut-off. Then out = x + amount × detail × mask, clamped to 0..1. In luminance mode the detail comes from BT.601 luma and is added equally to R, G and B, which changes brightness only. Source: core/sharpen.py and nodes/sharpen_node.py.

docs.title: Sub-Pixel Mask Refiner
docs.text:
Takes a jagged, hard-edged cutout mask and gives it a smooth, feathered edge, while keeping the middle of the subject fully opaque and the background fully clear.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → mask → Sub-Pixel Mask Refiner Good for Softening SAM or rembg cutouts, removing the "sticker" look, preparing a mask for compositing

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
A binary mask has only two values: 0 (not selected) and 1 (selected). Every edge pixel is either in or out, so the edge looks stair-stepped and pasted on. A soft mask (also called an alpha) has in-between values along the edge, which blends the subject into the new background.

A plain blur would soften the edge, but it would also eat into the subject and let the background bleed in. This node is smarter: it marks a safe zone inside the subject and a safe zone outside it, and only feathers the thin band between them. Use it when your mask is already roughly in the right place and you only need a better edge. If the edge has to follow fine detail like hair, use Edge-Aware Mask Refiner or Alpha Matte instead.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Load Image → Convert Image to Mask (or any node that outputs a mask).
  2. Connect the mask to Sub-Pixel Mask Refiner.
  3. Start with the defaults (erosion 2, dilation 4, feather 2.0). Raise feather_sigma for a softer edge.
  4. Check the result with Mask Preview.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip erosion_radius 2 How far to pull back from the edge to find the "definitely inside" core. That core stays fully white. 0 to 64. Bigger = a wider feathered band on the inside. dilation_radius 4 How far to push out from the edge to find the "definitely outside" zone. That zone stays fully black. Keep it equal to or larger than erosion_radius. feather_sigma 2.0 Softness of the edge, in pixels. 0.1 to 32. Try 1 to 4 for portraits. threshold 0.5 Values above this count as selected before anything else happens. Only matters if your input is not already pure black and white.

Output: refined_mask (MASK), same size as the input.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Feed it a clean binary mask. If the mask has specks or holes, run Mask Cleanup first.
  • Set dilation_radius a little larger than erosion_radius so the soft band is centred on the original edge.
  • Setting both radii to 0 turns the node into a plain Gaussian blur of the mask. That is rarely what you want.
  • For hair and fur, a feather alone is not enough. Build a Trimap and use Alpha Matte.
Under the hood

The mask is binarised with mask > threshold. A Gaussian blur of the binary mask gives the feather. An eroded copy is the inside core and 1 - dilated copy is the outside core. The output is inside + (1 - inside - outside) * feather, clamped to 0..1, so the feather only shows in the band between the two cores.

Erosion and dilation use a square window (a sliding max, done with separable max_pool2d), not a round one, so memory stays proportional to the image size even at large radii. The Gaussian kernel is sized to cover about three sigma. A warning is logged when more than 5% of the input pixels are mid-grey, because the node expects a near-binary mask. Source: core/mask_refiner.py.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Mask Cleanup for removing specks and holes before refining
  • Edge-Aware Mask Refiner for edges that follow the photo
  • Mask Edge Smoother for smoothing jagged edges while keeping corners
  • Mask Preview for checking the result

docs.title: Tone Curve
docs.text:
The familiar curves adjustment: bend the tonal response of the whole image or of a single colour channel, with ready-made presets or your own eight points.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → color → Tone Curve (RGB) Good for S-curve contrast, lifting or crushing shadows, fixing a colour cast channel by channel

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
A tone curve maps every input brightness to a new output brightness. A gentle S shape darkens the shadows and brightens the highlights, which adds contrast. Raising the lower part lifts shadows for a faded look. Applying a curve to only the red, green or blue channel changes colour balance, which is how you remove a cast or add a split-tone.

This node uses a curve through eight control points, smoothed with a Catmull-Rom spline, so it behaves smoothly and predictably.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Load Image → Tone Curve → Preview Image.
  2. Choose preset = s_curve_mild with channel = rgb_master.
  3. Lower strength to 0.6 if the effect is too heavy.
  4. For your own curve, set preset to custom and edit points_json.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip preset linear linear (no change), s_curve_mild, s_curve_strong, lift_shadows, crush_blacks or custom. S-curve for contrast, lift_shadows for a matte look. channel rgb_master rgb_master applies the same curve to red, green and blue (contrast). r, g or b applies it to that channel only (colour balance). Use single channels for casts. points_json a mild S-curve Your own eight points as [[x1,y1],…,[x8,y8]]. Used only when preset is custom. See rules below. strength 1.0 (0 to 1) Blend between the original (0) and the full curve (1). 0.5 to 0.8 for subtle grading.

Output: image_toned, the adjusted picture.

Rules for points_json: exactly 8 points; every value between 0 and 1; the first point is [0,0] and the last is [1,1]; the x values must strictly increase. Anything else raises an error with a clear message. Example (a mild S-curve):

[[0.0, 0.0], [0.15, 0.10], [0.30, 0.25], [0.45, 0.43],
 [0.55, 0.57], [0.70, 0.75], [0.85, 0.90], [1.0, 1.0]]

To lift the shadows, raise the y of the second and third point. To darken the highlights, lower the y of the sixth and seventh.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Take the S-curve in small steps. s_curve_mild at strength 0.7 is often all a portrait needs.
  • To cool the shadows and warm the highlights, apply channel = b with a lifted shadow curve, then r with a lifted highlight curve. Two Tone Curve nodes in a row works fine.
  • crush_blacks plus Luminosity Masking lets you deepen the shadows without touching skin.
  • Curves cannot add local detail. Use CLAHE Local Contrast for that.
  • To keep a curve as a reusable look, bake it into a LUT with HALD Identity and LUT Export.
Under the hood

The eight points are turned into a 1024-entry lookup table with a Catmull-Rom (cubic Hermite) spline; the endpoints are pinned to 0 and 1. Pixel values are looked up with linear interpolation. With rgb_master the table is applied to all three channels; with r, g or b only to that channel. The result is blended with the input by strength and clamped to 0..1. The curve is applied directly to the RGB values the node receives, not in linear light. Values outside 0..1 are clamped with a logged warning, and strength = 0 returns the input.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• ColorLab: Camera Raw style tone and colour in one node
  • Luminosity Masking: apply a curve only to shadows, midtones or highlights
  • HALD Identity and LUT Export: save a curve as a LUT
  • Color Matcher: match to a reference first, then fine-tune with curves

docs.title: Example workflow
docs.text: Tone Curve example workflow. It applies the s_curve_mild preset to the portrait. Copy workflows/sample_portrait.jpg into ComfyUI/input/. It uses only core ComfyUI nodes and this pack.

docs.title: Tone Match LUT
docs.text:
Give it a photo whose colour you love and it writes a LUT that pushes other images toward that look. No manual grading needed.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → color → Tone Match LUT (auto-gen .cube) Good for Copying the feel of a reference shot, making a house look, matching a set of photos to a hero frame

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Color Matcher matches one image to another, but only for that pair. Tone Match LUT does the same kind of colour transfer once and saves it as a .cube file. You can then apply the LUT to any number of photos with LUT Import, or open it in other apps that read Cube 1.0.

It captures overall colour and tone: the average colour, how widely the colours spread, and how they relate to each other. It does not copy local detail or content.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Connect Load Image (your reference) to reference.
  2. Leave level at 8. Set filename (for example hero_look.cube).
  3. Queue the prompt. The lut_path output shows the new file in ComfyUI/output/.
  4. Apply it with LUT Import. Copy the file to ComfyUI/input/ or use the full path.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip reference — The image whose look you want to capture. Choose a well-exposed frame with the colours you want. level 8 Detail of the LUT. Choices: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. 8 gives a 64-point cube, the standard for creative looks. filename tone_match.cube Output name. Relative names go to ComfyUI's output/ folder; .cube is added if missing. An existing file is overwritten. title Tone Match LUT Name stored inside the file. Name it after the reference.

Output: lut_path — the full path of the written file.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Pick a reference that is representative. A reference dominated by one colour (a sunset, a green field) gives a strong, one-sided LUT.
  • A grey or nearly colourless reference produces a LUT that changes almost nothing.
  • Always test with LUT Import at strength 0.6 to 0.8 first. Automatic matches can be stronger than they look in the reference.
  • If the match is close but not perfect, do small fixes with Tone Curve after the LUT.
Under the hood

An identity HALD at the chosen level is converted to LAB and passed through an MKL (Monge-Kantorovich linear) transfer: a 3 × 3 matrix derived from the covariance of the HALD's LAB samples and the reference's LAB samples, plus the reference mean. If either covariance is ill-conditioned, it falls back to a mean-only shift. Results are clamped to the LAB range and converted back to RGB. A reference that is almost uniform grey returns the identity. The graded HALD is written with the same exporter as LUT Export. Earlier versions used histogram or mean/std matching; the current method preserves cross-channel colour relationships.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Color Matcher — match two images directly, no file.
  • LUT Import — apply the generated .cube.
  • LUT Export — export a hand-built grade instead.
  • HALD Identity — the chart used inside this node.

docs.title: Example workflow
docs.text: Tone Match LUT example workflow. A golden-hour copy of the portrait is the reference. Tone Match LUT writes a .cube file to ComfyUI/output/ and its path goes straight into LUT Import, which applies it to the original. Copy workflows/sample_portrait.jpg into ComfyUI/input/. It uses only core ComfyUI nodes and this pack.

docs.title: Trimap Builder
docs.text:
Converts an ordinary mask into a trimap: a map with a sure-subject core, a sure-background area, and a band of "unknown" pixels around the edge where the real transparency has to be worked out.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → mask → Mask: Trimap Builder Good for Preparing the input for Alpha Matte, defining how wide the edge zone is

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
A trimap has exactly three values:

Value Meaning Shows as 0.0 Definitely background Black 0.5 Unknown: solve this Grey 1.0 Definitely subject White

Matting algorithms do not try to decide the whole picture. They only work out the grey band. The more accurately you place that band over hair, fur or other soft edges, the better the final cutout. This node draws the band automatically by shrinking the subject and the background away from the mask edge. Whatever is left between them becomes the unknown zone.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Get a rough mask from SAM, rembg or similar.
  2. Connect it to Trimap Builder. Start with fg_radius 4 and bg_radius 8.
  3. Check it with Mask Preview in heatmap mode: you should see three flat levels.
  4. Connect the trimap to Alpha Matte.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Tip fg_radius 4 How far to shrink the subject inward to get the sure-subject core. 1 to 64. Raise it for a wider unknown band on the inside. bg_radius 8 How far to shrink the background away from the edge to get the sure-background area. 1 to 64. Raise it where the mask is loose or hair sticks out. smoothing 0.0 Optional blur applied to the mask before it is split into zones. It rounds off jagged outlines. 0 to 16. 1 to 2 helps with ragged masks.

The width of the unknown band is roughly fg_radius + bg_radius.

Output: trimap (MASK) with the values 0.0, 0.5 and 1.0 only.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• Make bg_radius larger than fg_radius when the mask is tight and hair sticks out beyond it.
  • For hard-edged products, use small radii (2 to 4). A thin band leaves less room for errors.
  • Do not blur or resize a trimap afterwards. That creates in-between values, and Alpha Matte will reject it.
  • Clean the input mask with Mask Cleanup first, so stray specks do not each get their own unknown halo.
Under the hood

The input is clamped to 0..1 and optionally Gaussian-blurred (smoothing is the sigma). It is then thresholded at 0.5. The sure-subject core is the binary mask eroded by an elliptical kernel of radius fg_radius (OpenCV). The sure-background is the inverse mask eroded by radius bg_radius. Everything that is neither is 0.5. Runs on the CPU per batch item and returns to the input device. The input must be (B,H,W). Source: core/mask_trimap.py.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Alpha Matte, which consumes the trimap
  • Mask Morphology for growing or shrinking a mask by hand
  • Mask Cleanup to prepare the input mask
  • Mask Preview to inspect the three zones

docs.text: Trimap Builder example workflow. Copy workflows/sample_portrait.jpg and workflows/sample_binary_mask.png into ComfyUI/input/. It shows the sure-subject, unknown and sure-background bands built from the subject mask. It uses only core ComfyUI nodes and this pack.

docs.title: Unwrap Face
docs.text:
Puts an edited face crop back where it came from. It undoes the straightening done by Facial Aligner and blends the result into your original photo.

In ComfyUI Add Node → ComfyUI-JH-PixelPro → face → Unwrap Face (paste back) Good for Finishing an align → edit → paste-back chain; keeping the rest of the photo at full original quality

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: AI retouching, upscaling and face restoration work best on a small, upright, centred crop. Facial Aligner makes that crop and also gives you the exact inverse transform. Once the crop is edited, Unwrap Face uses that transform to rotate, scale and place it back on the full-size photo, so only the face area changes and the rest stays untouched.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Run Face Detect (or Face Detect Lite) and send landmarks_json to Facial Aligner.
  2. Edit the aligned crop (image_aligned) with your AI or retouch nodes.
  3. Connect the edited crop to edited_aligned, your original photo to original_image, and Facial Aligner's inverse_matrix_json to inverse_matrix_json.
  4. Check image_composited in a Preview Image. Adjust feather_radius if the edge shows.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default What it does Tip edited_aligned — The edited, aligned face crop. Keep it the same size as the aligner output. original_image — The full-size photo to paste into. The same image you detected on. inverse_matrix_json identity matrix The inverse transform from Facial Aligner. Always wire it. The default does nothing useful. feather_radius 16.0 (0–128) Softness of the edge, in pixels. 0 is a hard edge. Larger values hide the seam but soften the face edge. Ignored when mask_override is connected. mask_override optional Your own blend mask, full-size like the original. Use a face or skin mask to paste only the skin, not the whole crop. Output Type Meaning image_composited IMAGE The original photo with the edited face pasted in. mask_used MASK The blend mask that was applied.

docs.title: Tips from retouching
docs.text:
• By default the pasted area is the whole aligned square, softened by feather_radius. That includes hair and background in the crop. Connect a face or skin mask to mask_override to paste only the parts you want.
  • If your AI pass changes the crop's resolution, scale it back to the aligner's output size first, so the transform lines up.
  • Visible colour step at the edge? Match colours before pasting back with Color Matcher, or use Face Beauty Blend for a final, strength-controlled blend.
  • With a batch, edited_aligned, original_image and the matrix list must each have one entry or match the batch size.
Under the hood

The crop is warped onto the original canvas with kornia.geometry.transform.warp_affine, using the inverse matrix (3×3 or 2×3, one per image). Without mask_override, a white square the size of the crop is warped the same way, shrunk inward by 2 × feather_radius and blurred with a Gaussian (sigma = feather_radius), so the soft edge stays inside the crop and never picks up the empty padding around it. The result is mask × warped + (1 − mask) × original, clamped to [0, 1]. mask_override must match the original's height and width exactly. Inputs outside [0, 1] are clamped with a warning. The warp runs over the full canvas, so large images are slower on CPU than on GPU. The code lives in core/unwrap_face.py.

docs.title: Related nodes
docs.text:
• Facial Aligner — makes the crop and the inverse matrix.
  • Face Beauty Blend — a final masked blend with strength control.
  • Face Detect and Face Detect Lite — find the landmarks.
  • Face category overview

docs.title: PixelPro cho ComfyUI
docs.text:
Những kỹ thuật hậu kỳ bạn vẫn dùng hằng ngày (tách tần số, luminosity mask, LUT, chồng layer, tách nền chuẩn từng sợi tóc, căn khuôn mặt) nay thành 64 node chạy GPU ngay trong ComfyUI.

Bắt đầu Xem các node GitHub

docs.title: Vì sao chọn PixelPro
docs.text:
• Kỹ thuật retouch thật

    Không phải bộ lọc đặt tên kêu. Tách tần số (frequency separation), luminosity mask, khớp màu trong LAB, hòa trộn theo kim tự tháp Laplacian và tách alpha closed-form đều hoạt động đúng như người làm hậu kỳ mong đợi.

  • Ưu tiên GPU, vẫn chạy được trên CPU

    Xây dựng trên PyTorch và Kornia. Các bộ lọc nặng chạy trên CUDA và luôn giữ bộ nhớ trong giới hạn. Máy chỉ có CPU vẫn chạy được, chỉ chậm hơn.

  • Ăn khớp với quy trình AI

    Căn khuôn mặt, chạy inpaint hay ControlNet, rồi dán lại liền mạch. Dựng mask cho bất kỳ công cụ phân vùng nào và kiểm tra kết quả bằng SSIM/PSNR.

  • Kiểm thử kỹ, tài liệu đầy đủ

    Hơn 800 test tự động, workflow mẫu cho từng node mới, và tài liệu song ngữ Anh – Việt.

docs.title: Chọn theo việc cần làm
docs.text:
• Màu & tông

    Chỉnh màu kiểu ACR, đường cong tông, khớp màu, nhập/xuất LUT và tăng tương phản cục bộ CLAHE.

  • Mask

    Từ mask phân vùng thô đến alpha sạch chuẩn từng sợi tóc: tinh chỉnh, tách alpha, dọn dẹp và xem trước.

  • Khuôn mặt

    Nhận diện mặt, 468 điểm landmark, chỉnh dáng, căn mặt rồi dán lại, kèm mask theo tông da.

  • Bộ lọc

    Tách tần số, làm mịn da giữ chi tiết và làm nét không viền màu.

  • Ghép ảnh

    Chồng layer kiểu Photoshop với 27 blend mode, và hòa trộn đa tần số không lộ đường nối.

  • Hình học

    Căn khuôn mặt, sửa méo ống kính và tự căn khớp ảnh chụp thứ hai.

  • Look màu

    Các look màu hoàn chỉnh chọn từ một danh sách, có thanh chỉnh cường độ.

  • Kiểm tra chất lượng

    Đo xem bản chỉnh đã thay đổi gì: SSIM, PSNR và bản đồ nhiệt vùng thay đổi.

docs.title: Một chuỗi retouch chân dung điển hình
docs.text:
Load Image
  → Face Detect Lite ──→ Facial Aligner ──→ (bước AI hoặc retouch của bạn) ──→ Unwrap Face
  → Frequency Separation / Skin Smoother  (da)
  → Smart Sharpen + Detail Mask            (mắt, tóc)
  → ColorLab hoặc LUT Preset               (màu)
  → QA Image Diff                          (kiểm tra kết quả)

Mỗi bước là một node. Hãy bắt đầu với Hướng dẫn nhanh, hoặc mở các ví dụ.
